title: Docker MCP Gateway
summary: Route your agent through Docker's MCP gateway so each tool server runs in its own isolated container with secrets kept out of env variables.
description: The Docker MCP gateway sits between your coding agent and a set of MCP servers. Instead of starting each server yourself, you pick them in a profile and the gateway runs the local ones in separate containers, with minimal access to your machine.

Your agent sees one server and the gateway handles the rest. You can also turn individual tools on or off per profile, which is a simple way to keep a risky tool out of reach. It needs Docker Desktop 4.59 or later with the MCP Toolkit enabled.
useWhen: Use several MCP servers without wiring each into every agent
Keep third-party MCP servers off your host by running them in containers
Restrict an agent to a short list of approved tools
Share one tool set between Claude Code and Cursor

mcp.name: docker
access: Starts containers for the MCP servers in your active profile
Exposes whichever tools those servers offer to your agent

example.prompt: List the tools you can reach through the Docker gateway and say which server each one comes from.
example.result: 12 tools from 3 servers in the default profile: fetch (1 tool), github (9 tools) and duckduckgo (2 tools). Each runs in its own container.

faq.question: Which servers does the agent get?
faq.answer: Those in the profile you run. With no flag it uses the default profile. Add --profile name to the args to pick another.

faq.question: Does it work without Docker Desktop?
faq.answer: Outside Docker Desktop you first run docker mcp feature enable profiles, as the repository describes.

faq.question: Where do server secrets go?
faq.answer: The gateway uses Docker Desktop's secrets handling, so you do not put tokens in the agent config.

access: Reach depends on the servers in your profile
